messages:
infra-alert-bot: ALERT: Multiple nodes in us-west-2a reporting repeated GPU driver resets (XID) and container OOMs. Affected autoscale pool: inference-prod-g4. Spike began ~5m ago. Auto-evac attempted: 3 nodes failed to drain cleanly.
maya (oncall): seeing it. loads of 'NvHostCtrl' and 'Xid 13' in dmesg. CPU mem fine but containers getting OOMKilled intermittently after driver resets.
devin (eng-sre): checking node health now. pulling logs. pls hold on rolling anything. tagging rahul for runtime context.
rahul (eng-runtime): thanks. quick note: we've seen noisy XID chains before when ECC correctable errors climb then driver self-reset. Could be thermal or mem parity.
ops-bridge-bot: /create-bridge incident-2820001111 --severity high --topic "gpu-driver-reset-chain"
sarah (cust-succ): I have a customer on a support call (AcmeCorp) noticing 500s on embeddings endpoint. They're asking for ETA.
maya (oncall): @sarah acknowledge; telling them we're investigating and routing to fallbacks.
devin (eng-sre): tail of dmesg from node ig-prod-07: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, 0x80300084
[ 1234.567891] NVRM: GPU at 0000:03:00: driver reset
[ 1234.568000] kernel: pid 32456 (python), uid 1001: oom_kill_process: Killed process 32456 (python) total-vm:1800000kB, anon-rss:1400000kB, file-rss:0kB
```
devin (eng-sre): node shows repeated Xid 31/13 in quick succession. nvml reports ECC corrected counts increasing.
rahul (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) drain with --ignore-daemonsets and prefer evicting heavy workers 3) route traffic off the pool to fallback model variant (cpu or smaller batch) 4) capture full nv-host traces and sysdiagnose tarball
maya (oncall): starting with cordon/drain on ig-prod-07, ig-prod-08. I'll run graceful evacs.
maya (oncall): kubectl cordon ig-prod-07 && kubectl drain ig-prod-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force || true
devin (eng-sre): note: one pod stuck in ContainerCreating due to nvidia-device-plugin failing after reset. We may need node-restart if plugin doesn't recover.
rahul (eng-runtime): while we evacuate, switch the inference routing policy to 'tier-burst' with fallback to 'open-small' model. I pushed a temporary override to routing config: ```json
{"pool":"inference-prod-g4","fallback_model":"open-small-v1","routing_mode":"prefer-healthy"}```
rahul (eng-runtime): saved as runbook step: rollback in 30m if stable.
sarah (cust-succ): communicated to AcmeCorp: "We observed transient GPU driver resets causing 500s on embedding endpoints. We have routed traffic to fallback models to reduce customer impact. Engineering is actively evacuating affected nodes." :thumbsup:
maya (oncall): after first two drains, ig-prod-09 also reported high corrected ECC counts; cordoned it as precaution.
devin (eng-sre): collecting metrics: 95th latency on embeddings spiked from 120ms -> 2.4s, errors up to 6% on the pool. Global routing reduced total 500s to 0.6% after override.
ops-bridge-bot: Bridge created: https://bridge.internal/incident/2820001111
rahul (eng-runtime): grabbing nv-hostdiag: ```bash
sudo nv-hostdiag --collect --output /tmp/nvdiag-2820001111.tar.gz
scp /tmp/nvdiag-2820001111.tar.gz eng-sre@logs:~
```
devin (eng-sre): running simultaneous step: restarting nvidia driver on three quarantined nodes in sequence to avoid cluster-wide impact. systemctl restart nvidia-driver || modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia
maya (oncall): restart on ig-prod-07 completed. node returned to Ready but kubelet reported plugin flaps; giving it 2 min then uncordon if stable.
rahul (eng-runtime): added extra nvml telemetry capture to ingestion for 60m. Also enabled verbose nvidia logs on nodes: /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf set to debug=1 (temporary).
devin (eng-sre): small config snippet for durable drains in runbook: ```yaml
- cordon: true
- drain: --timeout=600s --grace-period=30 --ignore-daemonsets
- restart-driver: true
```
devin (eng-sre): found kernel message suggesting ECC retries: "EDAC MC0: CE count increased" on the node. That points to hardware-correctable ECC events preceding driver reset.
rahul (eng-runtime): long term: schedule hardware health check for that rack, consider moving those GPUs to maintenance, and mark them for vendor RMA if we see a sustained CE->UE trend.
sarah (cust-succ): AcmeCorp wants a post-incident email. Can we confirm start/end + impact numbers? I can draft once we have final numbers.
maya (oncall): summary so far for handoff: - start: 2820001111 - affected pool: inference-prod-g4 - mitigations: traffic routed to fallback, cordoned 3 nodes, restarted drivers sequentially, nv-hostdiag collected - current state: pool healthy at 99.4% success after routing override, nodes under observation.
ops-bridge-bot: Reminder: Handoff checklist: /handoff next-oncall --summary "GPU driver reset chain; continue monitoring; verify nvml metrics"
maya (oncall): @devin @rahul I'm going offline in 25m. leaving next-oncall: devin. Please pick up and confirm final cleanup.
devin (eng-sre): taking over. I'll stay on bridge. Next steps: observe for 2x reset window (15m), if none, unroute fallback, uncordon nodes one by one, schedule maintenance window for full hardware sweep.
rahul (eng-runtime): noted. Also recommend creating an automated alert for CE rate > 5/min per node to preempt similar cascades. I'll file ticket INF-1428.
sarah (cust-succ): drafting customer note: "Start: 2026-03-15T03:15Z; Impact: transient 500s on embeddings for subset of requests; mitigation: traffic routed to fallback models, no data exfiltration; status: degraded -> stable; next: post-incident report with root cause and action items."
maya (oncall): handing off: devin oncall, ops bridge active, diagnostics uploaded to logs. If resets recur, escalate to hardware vendor and start RMA flow.
devin (eng-sre): handoff ack. capture final metrics and close the bridge when stable. I'll post a short incident summary here after observation window.
ops-bridge-bot: Bridge closed by devin at 2820001500 (observed stable).
maya (oncall): thanks team. follow-up notes: collect nv-hostdiag tarballs into incident artifact store and link to INF-1428. We'll include proposed alerting change and suggested thermal checks in the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
